title: Departing and Being with Christ
subtitle: Bible Readings — Chapter 111
deckName: Reading 111 - Departing and Being with Christ
titleConcept: the apostle Paul, a weathered older man of slight build with a balding head, a full greying dark beard and deep-set earnest eyes, in a plain brown wool robe, seen from a little distance standing at a high barred window of a Roman prison, chained, gazing out toward a dawn sky where the first golden light breaks through the clouds, the room in deep shadow

slides.text: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
slides.concept: the apostle Paul, a weathered older man of slight build with a balding head, a full greying dark beard and deep-set earnest eyes, in a plain brown wool robe, chained by the wrist to a Roman soldier in a bare stone prison room, writing on a scroll by the light of a high barred window, his face calm and resolved
slides.note: Written from prison. Christ magnified whether by life or by death (v. 20): the gain is for Christ's cause, not merely Paul's comfort.

slides.text: For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better:
slides.concept: the apostle Paul, a weathered older man of slight build with a balding head, a full greying dark beard and deep-set earnest eyes, in a plain brown wool robe, seated alone in a dim Roman prison cell, his chained hands resting on an unfinished scroll, his face lifted toward a shaft of light from a small high window, torn between longing and duty
slides.note: "Strait" (synechomai): pressed from both sides. "Depart" (analyo): loosing a ship from its moorings, striking a tent to move on. The verse does not say when or how he would be with Christ.

slides.text: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you.
slides.concept: the apostle Paul, a weathered older man of slight build with a balding head, a full greying dark beard and deep-set earnest eyes, in a plain brown wool robe in chains, dictating a letter to a young companion who writes on a scroll, a few believers from Philippi gathered close and listening with love and concern, warm lamplight in a plain stone room
slides.note: Paul chose to remain: not because death would be bad for him, but because his ministry was more needful for the church.

slides.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
slides.note: Paul's own timeline: Christ descends, the dead in Christ rise first, the living are caught up together with them, and so (houtos, in this manner) shall we ever be with the Lord.

slides.text: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
slides.note: Christ names the moment: I will come again, and receive you unto myself.

slides.text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
slides.note: The dead know not any thing. Whether eight hours or eight hundred years, the sleeper wakes as if it were a moment.

slides.text: His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.
slides.note: In that very day his thoughts perish. Paul's next conscious moment would be the presence of Christ at His coming.

slides.text: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
slides.note: Two thousand years on earth; for the sleeping saint, the twinkling of an eye. This is why departing is "far better."

slides.text: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
slides.concept: the apostle Paul, a weathered older man of slight build with a balding head, a full greying dark beard and deep-set earnest eyes, in a plain brown wool robe, older now and in a cold dark Roman dungeon, a worn cloak about his shoulders, writing his last letter by a guttering oil lamp, his face peaceful and ready
slides.note: Near the end of his life: the time of my departure is at hand.

slides.text: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
slides.concept: a radiant golden crown of righteousness resting on a white cloth upon a stone ledge in a shaft of heavenly light, a great multitude of the redeemed faintly glimpsed in glory beyond, warm golden light
slides.note: The crown is given "at that day," the day of His appearing, and to Paul together with all them that love His appearing, not before them.

slides.text: And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.
slides.concept: a quiet hillside burial garden at evening, an old labourer's tools laid down beside a simple sealed tomb, olive trees and long golden shadows, a feeling of deep rest and peace
slides.note: Death for the believer is rest from labour, not an intermediate state of waiting or uncertainty.

slides.text: These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
slides.note: Christ's own word for death is sleep, and He goes to awake him.

slides.text: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
slides.concept: Adam and Eve standing modestly in the garden of Eden before the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, listening reverently as a radiant heavenly light falls on them from above, lush garden and soft morning light, the figures seen from a little distance
slides.note: God said, Thou shalt surely die.

slides.text: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
slides.note: Satan contradicted: Ye shall not surely die. The lie of the soul's natural immortality opened the door to spiritualism, purgatory and prayers to the dead.

slides.text: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.
slides.concept: Jesus matching the reference character with long dark brown hair, short beard, white robe with gold-trimmed sleeves and golden sash coming in great glory upon a bright cloud above the earth, surrounded by a host of shining angels, people on the hills below lifting their faces and hands to him in joy
slides.note: Christ ministers in the heavenly sanctuary to prepare a people to meet Him. The reward is given at His appearing, not at death (Rev 22:12; 2 Cor 5:10).

slides.text: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.
slides.note: My reward is with me: no one receives his final destiny before the verdict is rendered.

slides.text: Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.
slides.note: Our comfort is not that loved ones are looking down, but that they rest securely until Jesus calls them forth.

slides.text: Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.
slides.concept: a dim candlelit room where a hooded medium leans over a table toward a pale glowing apparition, while in the foreground a grieving widow draws back clutching an open Bible to her breast, its pages catching a clean steady light
slides.note: If the dead are unconscious, any spirit claiming to be a departed loved one is a demonic deception.

slides.text: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
slides.note: We sorrow, but not as others which have no hope. Our loved ones in Christ are safe in His keeping.

slides.text: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.
slides.note: He who conquered the grave holds the keys.

slides.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
slides.note: Whether we live until His coming or sleep in death, our next conscious moment of meeting Jesus comes at the same glorious instant.

slides.text: Wherefore comfort one another with these words.
slides.concept: a small group of mourners at an open garden tomb at dawn, an older believer with his arm about a weeping young widow, pointing her gaze to the first light of sunrise breaking over the eastern hills, their faces turning from grief to hope
slides.note: Comfort one another with these words. Trust Him, live for Him, and look for that blessed hope.
